ins.title: Winding instructions
ins.subtitle: Frame {d} mm · {pins} pins · threads: {threads} · lines: {lines}
ins.how: Pins are numbered 1 to {pins}, clockwise as seen from the front, with pin 1 at the top (12 o'clock), as on the nail template. Tie each thread to its start pin, then run it from pin to pin in the order printed: along each row from left to right, row after row, down the left column first and then the next. A row holds ten pins; tick its box when it is done. The smaller number after the box is the step the row starts with. The time at the end of a row tells where its first pin is, read as the hour hand of a clock. Wind the threads in the order of this sheet: each one lies on top of those before it.

ins.empty: This thread has no lines: skip it.

drop.hint: Drop a picture or a project file
error.tooLarge: That file is larger than {mb} MB.
error.notImage: {name} is not a PNG, JPG or WebP picture.
error.folder: Drop a single file, not a folder.
error.noFile: That was a link, not a file. Save the picture first, then drop the file.
error.multiple: {n} files were dropped; the first one was opened.

error.internal: Something went wrong here. Nothing was lost; try again.
error.settings: These settings cannot be generated. Check the pins, the minimum skip and the line budgets.
error.project: That file is not an img2string project.

picture.privacy: The picture stays on this computer; nothing is uploaded.
picture.reopen: This project was saved without its picture. Open the picture again to change the result; what is already made can be used as it is.
picture.missing: The project came without its picture ({name}). Open it again to generate.
picture.different: This is a different picture from {name}; the crop was reset.
picture.small: This picture is only {w} × {h} px, so it will look soft. A larger one gives more detail.
crop.hint: Drag the picture to move it; scroll or pinch to zoom.
preset.mono-black: Black thread on a white board
preset.mono-white: White thread on a black board
preset.mono-black-white: Black, then white, on a white board
preset.colour-cmyk: Yellow, cyan, magenta, black on white
preset.colour-rgbw: Red, green, blue, white on black
preset.blackWhiteNote: The white thread is wound last and covers the black where the picture is light: more contrast, at about three times the lines and winding time.
thread.listHint: The first thread is wound first and lies at the bottom; later threads cover it.
thread.name: Thread name
thread.widthHint: The width the thread appears to have. Fuzz and shadow make thread look wider than its label says.
order.hint: Tries every winding order on a small version of the picture, then checks the best three at full size.
order.changed: The threads are now in the best order found: {percent}% of the error removed.
order.kept: This order is already the best: {percent}% of the error removed.
frame.spacing: Pins are {gap} mm apart. Near the centre a line can be placed to about {place} mm; fine detail comes from many lines crossing.
adjust.rangeHint: Lower darkness for fewer lines. Very light areas will still look grey, because every line crosses the whole circle.
importance.hint: Lines crowd near the rim, so backgrounds there look busy. Quiet rim lets the centre win.
gen.resHint: Pixels across the frame while computing. Higher is finer and slower.
gen.minSkipHint: Fewest pins between two consecutive pins; avoids short lines along the rim.
gen.alpha: One line covers {alpha} of a pixel it crosses (keep it at 0.5 or below).
issue.alpha: The thread is too thick for that resolution, so the resolution was lowered.
issue.min-skip: The minimum skip was lowered: a frame needs at least twice the skip plus one pins.
issue.frame: A frame value was out of range and was corrected.
issue.thread: The thread width was out of range and was corrected.
issue.generator: The resolution was out of range and was corrected.
issue.budget: A line budget was out of range and was corrected.
issue.thread-equals-board: The first thread has the board's colour, so its lines will not show. Wind it later, or change a colour.
issue.duplicate-thread: Two threads have the same colour.
issue.thread-colour: A thread colour was not a valid colour and was replaced.
issue.threads-count: Only the first six threads were kept.
issue.board-colour: The board colour was not a valid colour and was replaced.
issue.frame-shape: Only round frames are supported; the frame was read as a circle.
issue.crop: The crop was out of range and was corrected.
issue.adjust: An adjustment was out of range and was corrected.
issue.image: The picture's size in the file was not valid.
issue.importance: Some brush strokes in the file were not valid and were left out.
issue.player: The player's settings were out of range and were corrected.
issue.project-version: This project was saved by a different version; it was read as well as possible.
issue.result: The winding sequence in the file does not fit its settings and was left out.
issue.brush-png: The file's painted importance map is in a format this version does not read; it was left out.
run.empty: No line would bring the board closer to this picture: it is already as light as the board. Darken the picture, or choose other colours.
run.stopped: Stopped early. What is there can be used, or continued.
run.budget: The line budget ran out while lines would still help ({names}). Raise the budget, or lower the darkness.
run.unstarted: No line of {names} would help, so none was wound.
result.stale: The settings have changed since this result was generated.
stage.label: Picture and result
stage.targetHint: This is the picture the lines will try to match, inside the pin ring.
stage.cropHint: Drag to move the picture, scroll or pinch to zoom. The arrow keys, + and - work too.
stage.brushHint: Paint where the picture matters more (orange) or less (blue).
stage.modelHint: The quick preview: how dense the lines are in each spot.
stage.realisticHint: Every line drawn at its true width, in winding order.
stage.sideHint: The picture on the left, the result on the right.
stage.wipeHint: Drag the divider: the picture is on its left, the result on its right.
out.printHint: Print at 100% (actual size), then check the 100 mm bar with a ruler.
out.needResult: Generate first: the winding instructions come from the result.
player.title: Winding player
player.keys: Space, Enter or the right arrow: next. Left arrow: back. Steps are numbered as on the printed instructions: step 1 is the pin the thread is tied to.
player.clock: at about {clock} on the clock face
player.tieOn: Tie the thread to pin {pin}, then go to
player.changeThread: Cut and tie off. Tie {name} to pin {pin}, then go to
player.tieOff: Cut the thread and tie it off.
player.status: {n} of {total} lines · about {h} h {min} min left
project.embed: Keep the picture inside the project file
project.hint: The project file holds the settings and the winding sequence. Without the picture inside it, only its name and fingerprint are saved.
project.savedStale: Saved {name} with the settings its result was made from; your later changes are not in the file.
